title: Kale Caesar Salad with Massaged Leaves
changes_from_base: Same croutons and creamy anchovy dressing, but massaged raw kale replaces the romaine and is left to rest in the dressing for 20 minutes.
summary: This follows the classic Caesar method — the same croutons and creamy anchovy-mayonnaise dressing — but swaps romaine for massaged raw kale, which rests in the dressing for 20 minutes to soften further.
equipment: salad spinner or clean tea towels

ingredients.item: curly or cavolo nero kale (stems removed), torn into bite-size pieces
fine sea salt or table salt
ciabatta or day-old crusty white bread, cut into 2 cm cubes
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
fine sea salt or table salt
anchovy fillets in oil, drained, patted dry and mashed to a paste
garlic cloves, grated to a paste

steps.title: Massage the kale
steps.text: Wash and thoroughly dry the kale, then in the large bowl rub it with the olive oil and a pinch of salt. Squeeze and scrunch handfuls of leaves for about 2 minutes until the kale darkens slightly, shrinks a little and feels silky rather than tough. This breaks down the sturdy fibres in raw kale, so it becomes tender enough to eat without cooking.

steps.title: Bake the croutons
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Toss the bread cubes with the olive oil, grated garlic and a pinch of salt, spread on a tray and bake for 12-15 minutes, stirring once, until golden and crisp all the way through. Cool on the tray so they keep their crunch.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Whisk the lemon juice, mashed anchovy, garlic and mustard powder together, then whisk in the mayonnaise, grated cheese, olive oil and pepper until smooth. Using halal-certified mayonnaise rather than a raw egg yolk gives this dressing its classic thick, creamy texture while keeping it safe to eat. Taste and sharpen with more lemon juice if needed.

steps.title: Rest in the dressing
steps.text: Toss the massaged kale with three-quarters of the dressing and refrigerate for 20 minutes, up to 6 hours. Unlike delicate lettuce, kale actually improves as it sits in the dressing, softening further and taking on more flavour.

steps.title: Add croutons and serve
steps.text: Toss in the croutons, drizzle over the remaining dressing and scatter with the cheese shavings — check the pack for an animal-rennet-free hard cheese — and a grind of pepper. Serve straightaway while the croutons are still crisp.

tips: Massage the kale properly — skipping this step is the common mistake, leaving the leaves tough and bitter instead of tender.
Dry the kale thoroughly before massaging, or the oil won't coat it evenly.
Let the kale rest in the dressing for the full 20 minutes; this is what makes raw kale pleasant to eat.
Add the croutons only just before serving so they stay crisp rather than going soft in the dressing.
storage: Dressed kale (without croutons) keeps in the fridge for up to 1 day — add the croutons just before eating to keep them crisp. Store any extra croutons in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
